notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: I read the complete held EO 9811 (11 FR 14483, Dec. 17, 1946; the held extract also carries unrelated neighbouring Federal Register items). It is one operative sentence: under the 1887, 1906 and 1917 acts, trust or restriction periods against alienation in Indian-land patents that 'unless extended, will expire during the calendar year 1947' are 'extended for a further period of twenty-five years from the date on which any such trust would otherwise expire', excluding cases where Congress reserved the extension authority. It acts once on a closed class (periods expiring in 1947) and grants a fixed 25-year extension, so by its own term the extension it creates runs out no later than December 31, 1972; it contains no continuing command and no savings clause. The held own-term record TERM:EO:9811 (the 25-year operative sentence, read in the held full text) is the basis. The 1989 Codification row reads 'Authority maintained at departmental level (see EO 10250)', which I treat as a lead that the extension authority was later delegated to the Department of the Interior, not as a statement that EO 9811 itself is in force; EO 10250 is not held and I did not examine it. Whether specific trusts were later extended by Interior orders or statute is a separate question and does not make the 1946 presidential order itself a continuing command. Partial scope: only the 1947-expiring class and not congressionally reserved cases; the end applies to the whole order. This is a provisional NO hypothesis only; the exact last expiry date and any effect of EO 10250 or later statutes remain lifecycle gaps.
